questions.questionText: Why use withStructuredOutput with a Zod schema instead of just parsing the model's free-form text response yourself?
options: It's not actually different from manual text parsing
It constrains the model to produce arguments matching your schema and validates/parses the result, avoiding brittle regex-based text parsing
It makes the model respond faster
It only works with numeric data
questions.correctAnswer: It constrains the model to produce arguments matching your schema and validates/parses the result, avoiding brittle regex-based text parsing
questions.explanation: Rather than hoping the model's free text follows a parseable format, structured output constrains generation to match a schema and gives you a validated, typed object back.

questions.questionText: What is the single most important factor in whether an agent correctly decides to use a given tool?
options: The tool's function name in the source code
The tool's description, since that's the only signal the model has for deciding when the tool is relevant
How many arguments the tool's schema has
The order tools are defined in
questions.correctAnswer: The tool's description, since that's the only signal the model has for deciding when the tool is relevant
questions.explanation: The model never sees your implementation code — only the tool's name, description, and schema — so a vague description directly causes unreliable tool selection.

questions.questionText: What three things make up a LangChain tool definition?
options: A name, a description, and a schema plus the function to execute
Only a function, nothing else is needed
A prompt template and a chat model
A database connection and an API key
questions.correctAnswer: A name, a description, and a schema plus the function to execute
questions.explanation: A tool bundles a name and description (for the model to decide when/how to call it), a schema (defining valid arguments), and the actual function that runs when called.
